summary: Set 112 Session 3 of 3, the closing session: the tier removal is now PROVEN by a gate rather than asserted by a disposition, the release is staged, and the walk is stageable. THE GATE. ai_router/scripts/lightweight_resurrection_guard.py fails the build if any live file DECLARES the removed tier -- a tier: lightweight spec entry, a verificationMode / verification_mode field in any of its read or write forms, either mode value in an assigning position, or a reference to one of the five deleted modules -- and separately asserts the deleted module files and both Lightweight fixture trees are still absent. Wired into the Drift guards CI job and run by pytest. The design problem was never finding the strings; it was telling "declares the tier" from "explains why the tier is gone", because the removal deliberately leaves ~40 mentions behind (the migration message, its tests, the historical note, the cross-repo notice, the changelogs, the comments that say why a branch is missing). It classifies by POSITION, not by an allowlist of blessed files: comments, Python docstrings, markdown prose and inline backticks are narration and are never scanned; code outside comments, fenced code blocks and YAML/JSON bodies are declaration territory and always are. An allowlist was considered and rejected -- it ages into a blanket exemption, since anything could resurrect inside a listed file. Two escapes exist, both pinned by tests and printed on every run: the gate's own two files (which cannot hide a resurrection, because the deleted-file check reads the filesystem, not the text) and an opt-in frozen-history marker used by exactly one superseded notice. WHAT THE GATE CAUGHT ON ITS FIRST RUN: docs/cross-repo-migration-guard-notice.md -- a notice whose banner says everything else in it still applies -- told consumers to run ai_router.migrate_lightweight_to_canonical_v4 as step 2 of a 3-migrator chain, which S1 deleted; the superseded Set 048 notice said the same. Three stale present-tense claims went with them, including one in docs/session-constitution.md, a PRELOAD file, which still named verificationMode as a live gate-policy record. THE RELEASE, STAGED AND UNPUBLISHED: dabbler-ai-router 0.34.0 -> 1.0.0 (pyproject + __init__ + a [1.0.0] changelog section with a BREAKING banner), extension 0.49.0 -> 0.50.0 (a Set 112 section superseding the never-published 0.49.0), and repository-reference release-status rows. Every claim written into both changelogs was checked against the tree first. Publishing, tagging, and sending docs/cross-repo-lightweight-removal-notice.md are operator-gated and deliberately not done. THE WALK, AND THE GAP IT EXPOSED: the spec's first Look item is "the form shows no tier question", and the Getting Started form renders ONLY while a workspace has zero materialized session sets -- the fixture workspace ships four. The onboarding surface, the surface this set changed and the one a walk is most obviously for, was the one surface the stager could not stage. npm run walk -- --empty now stages it, PROVEN by npm run walk:smoke -- --empty (arg passthrough added) rather than asserted, with three Layer 2 tests pinning the mode. VERIFICATION: four rounds routed to gpt-5.5 (anthropic excluded), eight findings, ALL ACCEPTED AND FIXED, none disputed. Every round planted resurrection shapes in throwaway trees and watched the gate exit 0: round 1 caught compact JSON, a TS optional property, a dotted read, a PascalCase type alias, a semicolon-terminated constant, a single-line array, and -- sharpest -- an assigned triple-quoted Python spec template that the blanker was treating as a docstring (fixed with ast-based docstring detection); round 2 (supplementary) caught that .template scaffold sources were not scanned AT ALL, and spec.md.template is the canonical source of every new consumer repo's spec.md; round 3 caught destructuring and bracket reads; round 4 caught a bare-key object literal and a character class of mine (verification[_M]ode) that silently never matched verification_mode. Two findings were not about the gate and were pre-existing repo defects this session inherited: run_of_record declared the Layer 2 suite's command as npm test, the harness CONTRIBUTING documents as broken on Windows 11 + VS Code 1.120 and CI skips, so every session has recorded a run of record against a command it could not execute (fixed repo-wide); and repository-reference.md still named router 0.33.0 live when the changelog says 0.34.0 shipped 2026-07-15 -- and this session wrote a new row on top of that stale claim without checking it, the exact L-064-8 failure its own conventions block warns about. THE RESIDUAL, OPERATOR-ADJUDICATED: the loop reached its ENFORCED bound at round 4 and refused a fifth round, so the round-4 fixes are tested and probed but never independently re-read; three consecutive rounds each found one more shape. The gate catches every shape anyone has thought to plant and no one can prove that is all of them -- but its floor does not depend on the regexes, because the deleted-file check reads the filesystem and a returned module is caught however it is spelled. The operator accepted the close with the residual named. Runs of record after the last change: pytest 3,627 passed / 9 skipped; mocha 1,606 passing (npm run test:unit); Playwright 33 passed. drift_guard, tutorial_gate and the new resurrection guard all exit 0.

uat.attestation: Operator walked all 5 Look items and answered all 3 Decide items on 2026-08-09. Verdict PASS with one defect found -- the defect the walk exists for, since nothing in the suite could see it: the System Status strip warned about a missing provider API key on a brand-new project, before any provider path had been chosen. Operator: 'We shouldn't need that unless and until the user selects the direct api approach' and 'that should only become an issue when users select the direct API approach and the API Keys are not in the environment variables'. Fixed in-session: the fault now also requires workspaceInitialized, which keeps it firing for keyless direct-API users (an explicit api pick is never written to disk, so gating on a recorded choice would have silenced it for everyone it helps). Pinned by 4 Layer 2 cases and a Layer 3 falsifier on the empty-project window. Other items: Explorer rows 'it looks great'; the extension README implies no choice of tier; tier-model.md reads as 'honest history'. Decides: version 1.0.0 (operator may supply PyPI credentials at publish time); publish HELD until Set 114 completes; consumer notice NOT needed, since dabbler-homehealthcare-accessdb is the operator's own repo.
